Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

determination noun

firmness of purpose

also determined, be determined to, resolve (firmness), resolution (firmness), perseverance, persistence, single-mindedness

classical

Cic. Tusc. 4.37: quī moderātiōne et cōnstantiā quiētus animō est (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Fam. 9.11.1: firmitās et cōnstantia (Lewis & Short, s.v. firmitās)

cōnstantia, cōnstantiae f.

noun, first declension · Declension on Wiktionary

steadfastness, firmness of purpose

Firmness of character that holds to its course; it is also consistency and steadiness in general (see constant-steady, consistent).

Other words

  • persevērantia, persevērantiae f. — perseverance, persistence

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Cic. Inv. 2.164 (Lewis & Short); Caes. B.C. 3.26 (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

    Keeping on with what one has rightly decided; Cicero sets it against pertinācia, obstinacy in what one should give up (Inv. 2.165; see stubborn).

  • obstinātiō, obstinātiōnis f. — determination, resolve; obstinacy

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Prov. Cons. 41: quae ego omnia obstinātiōne sententiae repudiāvī (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

    Firmness in a good or a bad sense; obstinātō animō (or obstinātā mente) is “with a set mind, determinedly”.

  • certum est (mihi) — I am determined (to)

    phrase, with the infinitive · also used · classical · Enn. ap. Cic. Off. 1.38: eōrundem mē lībertātī parcere certum est (Lewis & Short, s.v. certus); Plaut., Ter. (Lewis & Short)

    (vōx sermōnis cotīdiānī: Plaut., Ter.)

    The spoken way to say “I’m determined to, I’ve made up my mind to”; Lewis & Short: mostly before Cicero, most frequent in Plautus.

Examples

  • persevērantia est in ratiōne bene cōnsīderātā stabilis et perpetua permānsiō

    perseverance is standing firm and lasting in a well-considered planCic. Inv. 2.164 (Lewis & Short)

  • sed obstinātā mente perfer, obdūrā

    but bear it with a set mind, hold outCatull. 8.11

  • Certum est mihi hoc hodiē perficere.

    I’m determined to finish this today.composed

See also stubborn, constant, consistent, decision.

SourcesLewis & Short: constantia · Lewis & Short: perseverantia · Lewis & Short: obstinatio · Lewis & Short: certus · Lewis & Short: firmitas
